issues.passage: The keynote was crafted to derogate the scientist for her careful, widely cited research.
issues.why: Transitive derogate = disparage is valid here: the keynote is crafted to speak down of the scientist. Odd motive does not make the wording a misuse; a student who knows the definition would accept the passage.

fix.correctPassage: Nothing in the agreement should derogate from existing labor rights.
wrongPassages: The keynote was crafted to derogate the scientist with awards celebrating her careful, widely cited research.
Conservators hoped to derogate the damaged fresco by restoring its original colors.
Alumni rose to derogate the retiring dean with tributes and a standing ovation.

issues.passage: Editors claimed to scrutinize the manuscript after skimming only the abstract.
issues.why: "Claimed to scrutinize" correctly uses scrutinize = examine closely and thoroughly. That the claim is false (they only skimmed) is pragmatic irony, not misuse of the word; a student who knows the definition would accept the wording as valid usage.

fix.correctPassage: Peer reviewers will scrutinize every claim before the paper is accepted.
wrongPassages: Editors scrutinized the manuscript by glancing at the title and never reading a sentence.
She scrutinized the contract for a few seconds and signed without reading further.
To scrutinize the budget, the committee approved it without opening a single page.
